'''Raymond Baker''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRS}} (born 1 November 1936)<ref name="whoswho"/> is a British chemist and former [[Chief executive officer|Chief Executive]] of the [[Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council]].<ref name="whoswho"/>

==Education==
Baker was educated at [[Ilkeston Grammar School]] and the [[University of Leicester]], where he gained his [[PhD]] for research titled "''[[Tritiated water|Detritiation Reactions]] in [[Aromaticity|Aromatic Systems]]''" in  1962.<ref name="bakerphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Raymond|last=Baker |title=Detritiation Reactions in Aromatic Systems |publisher=University of Leicester |date=1962 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0I_uSAAACAAJ|author-link=Raymond Baker (chemist)}}</ref>

==Career==
After completing his PhD, Baker did [[postdoctoral research]] at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] from  1962–64. He was appointed a [[lecturer]] in Organic Chemistry at the [[University of Southampton]] in 1964, [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] in 1974 and a [[Professor]] in 1977. Baker is a co-author of the textbook ''Mechanism in Organic Chemistry''.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Boche | first1 = G. | title = Book Review: Mechanism in Organic Chemistry. By R. Alder, R. Baker, and J. M. Brown | doi = 10.1002/anie.197306804 | journal = Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English | volume = 12 | issue = 8 | pages = 680–681 | year = 1973 }}</ref>

==Awards==
Baker was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1994 and [[Order of the British Empire|Commander of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire (CBE)]] in 2002.
